bibliographic.title: From setting to vetting: using artificial intelligence for Single Best Answer questions review
bibliographic.authors: Olivia Ng; Siew Ping Han; Magdalene Hui Min Lee; Dong Haur Phua
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ng, O., Han, S. P., Lee, M. H. M., & Phua, D. H. (2026). From setting to vetting: using artificial intelligence for Single Best Answer questions review. Korean Journal of Medical Education, 38(1), 10–14. https://doi.org/10.3946/kjme.2025.068

methodology.study_design: cross-sectional study comparing AI-based QA-bot ratings with two experienced medical educator raters on a shared rubric
methodology.sample_description: 32 AI-generated Single Best Answer (SBA) questions across clinical domains; evaluated by QA-bot (custom GPT/GPT-4o) and two experienced educators
methodology.technology_context: custom GPT QA-bot (GPT-4o) embedded with 25 criteria aligned with Bloom's taxonomy for rubric-based vetting of AI-generated SBA assessment items

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Study addresses LLM-assisted quality assurance of medical education assessment items, not governance of conversational LLM-based systems in regulated environments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: The article empirically evaluates an LLM-based QA-bot for vetting SBA questions and emphasizes human oversight as essential for educational and clinical relevance. However, the provided text contains no focus on conversational AI, chatbots/agents for end users, or governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, audit, compliance, contestation, or post-deployment monitoring of conversational systems. The human oversight described is a first-pass review workflow for assessment items, which falls outside the review's conversational governance scope despite LLM use in a regulated education domain.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is clear from purpose, methods, and conclusion in the supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Clear feasibility/reliability objective and appropriate ICC/Cronbach's alpha reporting for inter-rater comparison. Ethics, limitations, and fuller methodological detail are not visible in the excerpt provided.

cerqual.explanation: Methods appear internally coherent for an educational QA reliability study, but relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is very low based on the supplied text.

coding.theme: LLM-supported quality assurance for medical education assessment items
coding.subtheme: human oversight in AI-assisted question vetting

synthesis.main_claim: An LLM-based QA-bot can serve as an efficient first-pass reviewer of AI-generated SBA questions with good alignment to human raters, but human oversight remains essential for educational and clinical relevance.
synthesis.contribution: Empirical feasibility and reliability evidence for using a customized GPT-4o QA-bot with a 25-criterion Bloom-aligned rubric to vet medical education assessment items.
synthesis.limitations: AI was less consistent in detecting irrelevant complexity and accurately judging difficulty; human oversight still required. Full limitations section not provided in excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance; may serve only as peripheral contextual reference on human oversight in LLM-assisted review workflows if explicitly scoped beyond conversational systems.
